title: True feasts, watchfulness, and the path to knowledge
english: Do not say, “Today is a feast, so I will drink wine, and tomorrow is Pentecost, so I will eat meat.” Monks have no feast that consists in filling a man's belly.
The Lord's Passover is a crossing over from evil, and his Pentecost is the resurrection of the soul.
God's feast is forgetfulness of wrongs, but mournings will seize the one holding resentment.
The Lord's Pentecost is the resurrection of love, and the one who hates his brother will fall with a staggering fall.
God's feast is true knowledge, but the one who pays attention to false knowledge will die shamefully.
Better is fasting with a pure heart than a feast in an unclean soul.
The one who destroys evil thoughts from his heart is like the one dashing his infants against the rock.
A sleepy monk will fall into evils, but the one who stays awake will be like a sparrow.
Do not give yourself over to empty stories during watchfulness, and do not push away spiritual words, because the Lord watches your soul and will not leave you unpunished for any evil.
Much sleep thickens the mind, but good watchfulness makes it fine.
Much sleep brings on temptations, but the one who stays awake will escape them.
As fire melts wax, so good watchfulness melts evil thoughts.
Better is a man sleeping than a monk staying awake over vain thoughts.
An angelic dream gladdens the heart, but a demonic dream throws it into confusion.
Repentance and humility raise up the soul, and mercy and gentleness make it stand firm.
Remember always your departure and do not forget the eternal judgment, and there will be no transgression in your soul.
If a spirit of listlessness comes upon you, do not leave your house and do not turn aside at a time when it is again profitable. For as one whitens silver, so your heart will be made bright.
A spirit of listlessness drives away tears, and a spirit of grief crushes prayer.
The one who desires money will have many worries, and the one who holds on to it will mourn bitterly.
Do not let a scorpion linger in your bosom, nor an evil thought in your heart.
Do not be afraid to kill the offspring of snakes, and do not torment the thoughts of their hearts.
As fire tests silver and gold, so temptations test the heart of a monk.
Strip pride from yourself and put vainglory far away from you. For the one who fails to obtain glory will be grieved, and the one who obtains it will become proud.

Do not give your heart to pride, and do not say before the face of God, “I am strong,” so that the Lord does not abandon your soul and evil demons humble it. For then your enemies will terrify you through the air, and fearful nights will follow you.
Knowledge guards the way of life of a monk, but the one who descends from knowledge will fall among robbers.
From a spiritual rock flows a river, and an active soul will drink from it.
A pure soul is a vessel of election, but an unclean soul will be filled with bitterness.
Without milk a child will not be nourished, and without freedom from passions the heart will not be lifted up.
Freedom from passions leads the way before love, and love before knowledge.
Wisdom is added to knowledge, and prudence gives birth to freedom from passions.
The fear of the Lord begets prudence, and faith in Christ grants the fear of God.
A fiery arrow sets the soul ablaze, but an active man will quench it.
Knowledge turns away from shouting and blasphemy, and wisdom flees deceitful words.
Honey is sweet and the honeycomb is sweet, but knowledge of God is sweeter than both.

Listen, monk, to the words of your father, and do not make his admonitions void. Whenever he sends you, lead him and accompany him in your mind. For in this way you will escape evil thoughts, and evil demons will not prevail against you.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius continues his sayings to the monk, contrasting true Christian feasts with bodily indulgence and urging watchfulness, repentance, and obedience to one's spiritual father.

title: Community stewardship and the monk's inner discipline
english: If someone entrusts silver to you, do not scatter it, and even if you put it to work, give it back.
A wicked steward will oppress the souls of the brothers, and a resentful man will not have mercy on them.
Whoever scatters the monastery's possessions wrongs God, and whoever neglects them will not go unpunished.
An unjust steward will distribute badly, but a just one will give according to what each deserves.
Whoever speaks evil of his brother will be destroyed utterly, and whoever neglects a sick brother will not see light.
Better is a worldly man who serves a brother in weakness than a recluse who has no pity on his neighbor.
A foolish monk will neglect the tools of his craft, but a prudent one will take care of them.
Do not say, 'Today I will stay and tomorrow I will go out,' because you have not reasoned about this with wisdom.
A monk who wanders about will speak false words, and he will deceive his own spiritual father.
Whoever adorns his clothes and fills his belly feeds shameful thoughts, and he will not sit in council with the self-controlled.
If you enter a village, do not go near women and do not linger in conversation with them. For just as if someone swallowed a fishhook, so your soul will be dragged away.
A patient monk will be loved, but one who provokes his brothers will be hated.
The Lord loves a gentle monk, but he will push away the brash one.
A listless monk will grumble often, and a sleepy one will use his headache as a pretext.
If your brother is grieving, comfort him, and if he is in pain, suffer with him. For by doing this you gladden his heart, and you will heap up a great treasure in heaven.

A monk who fails to keep the words of his spiritual father will blaspheme the gray hair of the one who begot him and speak evil of the lives of his spiritual father's other disciples, and the Lord will despise him.
Whoever seeks a pretext separates himself from the brothers, and he will blame his own spiritual father.

Do not give ear to words against your spiritual father, and do not stir up the soul of one who dishonors him, so that the Lord may not be angry at your deeds and blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 68:29 LXX / 69:28 Hebrew).
Whoever obeys his spiritual father loves himself, but whoever contradicts him will fall into evils.
Blessed is the monk who keeps the commandments of the Lord, and holy is the one who preserves the words of his spiritual fathers.
A listless monk will suffer many losses, and if he grows negligent he will add even his monastic habit to those losses.
Whoever guards his tongue cuts straight his ways, and whoever watches over his heart will be filled with knowledge.
A double-tongued monk troubles the brothers, but a truthful one brings stillness.
Whoever trusts in his own self-control will fall, but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
Do not give yourself to filling your belly, and do not be filled with sleep at night. For in this way you will become pure, and the Spirit of the Lord will come upon you.
While one sings psalms, anger grows still, and while one is patient, he will be unafraid.
From gentleness knowledge is born, and from brashness ignorance.
Just as water makes a plant grow, so the humbling of anger lifts up the heart.
While one tracks down banquets, his lamp will be extinguished, and his soul will see darkness.
Weigh your bread on a scale and drink your water by measure, and the spirit of fornication will flee from you.
Give wine to the old and offer food to the sick, because they have worn out the flesh of their youth.
Do not trip up your brother, and do not rejoice over his fall. For the Lord knows your heart and will hand you over on the day of death.
A prudent monk will have freedom from passions, but a foolish one will pour out evils.
The Lord blinds a wicked eye, but he rescues the simple one from darkness.
As the morning star in heaven and as a palm tree in paradise, so is a pure mind in a gentle soul.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius continues his sayings to monks in community, now warning about stewardship of goods, treatment of brothers, and the inner disciplines that lead to knowledge.

title: Wisdom, Knowledge, and the Path of the Monk
english: A wise man will search out the words of God, but a fool will mock them.
The one who hates knowledge of God and pushes away contemplation of Him is like a man piercing his own heart with a spear.
Knowledge of the Holy Trinity is better than knowledge of bodiless beings, and contemplation of the Holy Trinity is better than the words of all the ages.
The gray hair of elders is gentleness, and their life is knowledge of the truth.
A gentle young man endures many things, but who will endure a fainthearted old man? I have seen an irascible old man exalting himself on his throne, yet his young man had more hope than he did.
The one who scandalizes worldly people will not go unpunished, and the one who provokes them dishonors his own name.
Fire will consume the one who troubles the church of the Lord, and the earth will swallow the one who opposes a priest.
The one who loves a bee will eat its honeycomb, and the one who gathers it will be filled with the Spirit.
Honor the Lord and you will know the words of bodiless beings; serve Him and He will show you the words of the ages.
Without knowledge the heart will not be lifted up, and a tree will not bloom without drink.
The flesh of Christ is the active virtues, and the one who eats it will become free from passions.
The blood of Christ is contemplation of created things, and the one who drinks it will be made wise by it.
The breast of the Lord is knowledge of God, and the one who reclines on it will be a theologian.
A knower and a man of active life met one another, and the Lord stood between them both.
The one who has acquired love has acquired a treasure, and he has received grace from the Lord.
Wisdom recognizes the doctrines of demons, and prudence tracks out their cunning.

Do not reject the holy doctrines that your fathers established, and do not abandon the faith of your baptism; do not push away the spiritual seal, so that the Lord may be in your soul and shelter you on the evil day.
The words of heretics are angels of death, and the one who receives them destroys his own soul.

Now then, my son, listen to me: do not approach the doors of lawless men or walk on their snares, lest you be caught. Keep your soul far from false knowledge. For I have spoken to them many times, and I have tracked out their dark words, and I have found the venom of asps in them. There is no prudence and no wisdom in their words. All who receive them will perish, and those who love them will be filled with evils. I have seen the fathers of their doctrines, and I have encountered them in the desert. For enemies of the Lord met me, and demons contended with me in words, and I saw no true light in their sayings.
A man who lies will fall away from God, and the one who deceives his neighbor will fall into evils.
The paradise of God is better than a garden of vegetables, and the river of the Lord is better than a great river that darkens the earth.
Heavenly water is more trustworthy than the water of Egyptian wise men drawing from the earth.
Just as those who climb wheels go downward, so those who exalt their own words are humbled in them.
The wisdom of the Lord lifts up the heart, and His prudence purifies it.
The words of providence are dark, and the contemplations of judgment are hard to understand, but a man of active life will recognize them.
The one who purifies himself will see intelligent natures, and a gentle monk will recognize the words of bodiless beings.
The one who says the Holy Trinity is a creature blasphemes God, and the one who rejects His Christ will not know Him.
Contemplations of the worlds widen the heart, and words of providence and judgment lift it up.
Knowledge of bodiless beings raises the mind and presents it to the Holy Trinity.
Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord, and do not forget my humble soul in the time of prayer.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius is closing his collection of sayings for monks in community, contrasting true knowledge of God with heretical teachings and urging the monk to hold fast to the faith he received.
